title: In Town: Finding a Place
overview:
Name the places in a town.
Stop a person politely and ask the way.
Understand left, right and straight on.
Check the answer before you go.
functions: Name the places in a town
Stop a person politely with excuse me
Understand left, right and straight on
Check an answer by saying it back
Ask a person to slow down or repeat
learningPath: Patterns: excuse me, where is, and turn left.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 13. Finding a place.
This unit is for the street.
First, places. Listen.
A shop. A market. A school. A bank.
A street. A bus stop. A station.
Say them with me.
Now the most important two words today.
Excuse me.
You say them before you ask a stranger.
Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
Say it with me. Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
Now the answer. Three directions.
Left. Right. Straight on.
Say them with me. Left. Right. Straight on.
Turn left. Turn right. Go straight on.
And two more words.
The corner. It is on the corner.
Far. Is it far? No, it is near.
Now the part people forget.
You must CHECK the answer.
They say: turn left at the corner.
You say: turn left at the corner? Thank you.
Say the answer back. Every time.
If it was fast, say: slowly, please.
If you did not hear, say: again, please.
That is Unit 13. Go and ask the way.

grammar.title: Excuse me, where is...?
grammar.explanation:
Two parts. The excuse me matters as much as the question.
Without it, you sound like you are giving an order.
grammar.rule:
Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
Excuse me. Where is the station, please?

Excuse me  +  Where is the ___  +  please

For more than one: Where ARE the toilets?
grammar.workedExample:
You are lost and you need the station.
1. Wait until the person looks at you.
2. Say: Excuse me.
3. Then: Where is the station, please?
4. Listen to the whole answer.
5. Then say it back to check.
grammar.mistake:
Do not start with the question alone.
Where is the bank? with no excuse me sounds sharp.
Two words fix it.
grammar.tip: Excuse me first. Please at the end.
grammar.practice:
Ask for each place.
1. the bank
2. the station
3. the market
4. the toilet
grammar.answers:
Excuse me. Where is the bank, please? and so on.
Check: excuse me at the start of all four?
Check: please at the end?

grammar.title: Left, right, straight on
grammar.explanation:
Three answers cover most directions.
Learn them with your hands, not your eyes.
grammar.rule:
Turn left.
Turn right.
Go straight on.

It is on the left.
It is on the right.
It is on the corner.

turn = change direction
go straight on = do not turn
grammar.workedExample:
Someone says: turn left at the corner.
1. Find the corner first.
2. Then turn left there.
3. Point with your hand as they speak.
4. That fixes it in your head.
5. Then say it back to check.
grammar.mistake:
Do not nod without understanding.
Point with your hand instead.
If your hand is wrong they will tell you.
grammar.tip: Use your hand while they talk.
grammar.practice:
Turn, go or on?
1. ___ left at the bank.
2. ___ straight on.
3. It is ___ the right.
4. ___ right at the corner.
grammar.answers:
1. Turn
2. Go
3. on
4. Turn
All four? You can follow a direction now.

grammar.title: Say it back
grammar.explanation:
This is the half of the lesson people skip.
Asking is easy. Understanding the answer is the hard part.
grammar.rule:
They say:  Turn left at the corner.
You say:   Turn left at the corner? Thank you.

They say:  It is on the right, next to the bank.
You say:   On the right, next to the bank? Thanks.
grammar.workedExample:
You asked and they answered fast.
1. Do not say thank you and walk away.
2. Say the main part back.
3. Your voice goes up, like a question.
4. They will say yes, or they will fix it.
5. Now you can go.
grammar.mistake:
A nod is not checking.
Nod when you were wrong, and you go wrong.
Saying it back takes three seconds.
grammar.tip: Say it back, then thank them.
grammar.practice:
Say each answer back.
1. Turn left at the bank.
2. Go straight on to the corner.
3. It is on the right.
4. It is next to the market.
grammar.answers:
1. Turn left at the bank?
2. Straight on to the corner?
3. On the right?
4. Next to the market?
All four? This one habit will save you many wrong turns.

grammar.title: Can you show me?
grammar.explanation:
Unit 3 gave you again and slowly, for words.
In a street you have a better move.
Ask for the answer in another FORM.
grammar.rule:
Can you show me?        (they point, or walk with you)
Can you write it, please?
Can you show me on the map?

Words are hard. A hand and a map are not.
grammar.workedExample:
They gave directions and you caught nothing.
1. Asking again gives you the same words.
2. So change the form instead.
3. Say: Sorry. Can you show me?
4. Most people point, or walk a few steps with you.
5. Still unsure? Say: Can you write it, please?
grammar.mistake:
Do not ask for the same words three times.
The third time will sound the same as the first.
Ask to SEE it instead.
grammar.tip: A hand beats a sentence when you are lost.
grammar.practice:
What do you say?
1. You want them to point. ___
2. You want it on paper. ___
3. You have a map with you. ___
4. You want the street name written. ___
grammar.answers:
1. Can you show me?
2. Can you write it, please?
3. Can you show me on the map?
4. Can you write it, please?
All four? You have a way out when words fail.

readings.title: Excuse Me, Where Is the Bank?
readings.setting: A street corner, in the morning
readings.passage:
Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
Go straight on to the corner.
Then turn left.
Straight on, then turn left?
Yes. The bank is on the right.
On the right. Is it far?
No, two minutes.
Thank you very much.
You are welcome.

readings.title: The Way to My Home
readings.setting: Written for a friend who is visiting
readings.passage:
Come out of the station.
Turn right.
Go straight on to the market.
Turn left at the market.
My street is the second on the right.
My house is on the corner.
It is a brown door.
It is not far. Ten minutes.
Call me if you are lost.

comprehension.a: Go straight on to the corner.
comprehension.why: Line 2: Go straight on to the corner.

The sign: Toilets left, behind the shop.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Name the places
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
shop ... market ... school ... bank
street ... bus stop ... station
Now say which ones are near your home.
Tap the mic. Name all seven places.
Then say three that are near you.
Check: seven places?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name three places in a town. Say what you do at each.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Excuse me
speaking.instructions:
Say each one. Start with excuse me every time.
1. Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
2. Excuse me. Where is the station, please?
3. Excuse me. Where is the toilet, please?
4. Excuse me. Is this the bus stop?
Tap the mic. Say all four.
Check: excuse me at the front of all four?
speaking.tutor: Stop the tutor with excuse me. Ask where two places are.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Left, right, straight on
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Point with your hand. Then say it.
1. Turn left.
2. Turn right.
3. Go straight on.
4. It is on the left.
5. It is on the right.
6. Turn left at the corner.
Tap the mic. Say all six.
Check: did your hand move each time?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for two directions. Point as it says them.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Say it back
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B. Say the answer BACK each time.
1. A: Turn left at the bank. B: Turn left at the bank? Thank you.
2. A: Go straight on to the corner. B: Straight on to the corner? Thanks.
3. A: It is on the right. B: On the right? Thank you.
4. A: Next to the market. B: Next to the market? Thanks.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: did your voice go up at the end?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor the way somewhere. Say every answer back to check it.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Slowly please
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: (says directions fast) B: Sorry. Slowly please.
2. A: (says them again) B: Again please. The last part.
3. A: Turn left at the market. B: Left at the market? Thank you.
4. A: Yes. B: Thanks a lot.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: did you ask twice without giving up?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to give fast directions. Ask it to slow down.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The way to your home
speaking.instructions:
Give directions from a bus stop to your home.
Use four lines.
Start with: Come out of the bus stop.
Use turn, straight on, left and right.
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: could a stranger follow them?
speaking.tutor: Give the tutor directions to your home. Ask it to say them back.

writing.title: Writing 1 — The way to my home
writing.prompt:
Write four lines of directions.
From the bus stop or the station to your home.
writing.model:
Come out of the station.
Turn right.
Go straight on to the market.
My street is the second on the left.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
At least one turn.
At least one straight on.
A stranger could follow them.
writing.extension: Add a line saying how long it takes.

writing.title: Writing 2 — Places near me
writing.prompt:
Write four lines about your town.
Say where four places are.
writing.model:
The shop is near my home.
The bank is on the corner.
The station is far.
The bus stop is on the right.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
Four different places.
A place word in each line, like near or far.
writing.extension: Add a line saying which place you go to most.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Which place?
activities.instructions:
Where do you go?
1. To buy food. ___
2. To get money. ___
3. To take a train. ___
4. Children learn there. ___
5. To wait for a bus. ___
6. Many people sell fruit there. ___
7. It has buildings on both sides. ___
activities.answers:
1. the shop
2. the bank
3. the station
4. the school
5. the bus stop
6. the market
7. the street
Five or more right: good.
activities.solo: Say your answers out loud first.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Turn, go or on?
activities.instructions:
Write turn, go or on.
1. ___ left at the bank.
2. ___ straight on.
3. It is ___ the right.
4. ___ right at the corner.
5. ___ straight on to the market.
6. It is ___ the left.
activities.answers:
1. Turn
2. Go
3. on
4. Turn
5. Go
6. on
Five or six right: good.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Ask it politely
activities.instructions:
Ask where each place is. Start with excuse me.
1. the bank
2. the station
3. the toilet
4. the market
5. the bus stop
6. the school
activities.answers:
Excuse me. Where is the bank, please? is the model.
Check: excuse me at the front of all six?
Check: please at the end?
Six done: you can stop a stranger politely.
activities.solo: Record all six, then listen back.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Say it back
activities.instructions:
Say each answer back as a question.
1. Turn left at the bank.
2. Go straight on to the corner.
3. It is on the right.
4. Next to the market.
5. The second street on the left.
activities.answers:
1. Turn left at the bank?
2. Straight on to the corner?
3. On the right?
4. Next to the market?
5. The second street on the left?
Four or five right: this habit will save you many wrong turns.
activities.solo: Say each one out loud with your voice going up.

activities.title: Practice 5 — What do you say?
activities.instructions:
Choose the right sentence.
1. They spoke too fast. ___
2. You heard nothing. ___
3. You want to see it on a map. ___
4. You want it written down. ___
5. You want to stop a stranger. ___
activities.answers:
1. Slowly please.
2. Again please.
3. Can you show me?
4. Can you write it, please?
5. Excuse me.
Four or five right: you can keep a conversation going.
activities.solo: Say your answers out loud first.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Read the sign
activities.instructions:
Look at Where Things Are in Reading 3.
1. Which way is the station?
2. Which way is the bank?
3. Where are the toilets?
4. Where is the bus stop?
5. Which way is the market?
activities.answers:
1. Straight on
2. Right
3. Left, behind the shop
4. Right, on the corner
5. Left
Four or five right: you can read a street sign.
activities.solo: Look at the sign, then answer.

quizzes.q: You go there to get money. It is the ___.
quizzes.why: A bank is for money. A market is for buying things.

quizzes.q: You wait there for a bus. It is the ___.
quizzes.why: A bus stop is where the bus stops for you.

quizzes.q: What do you say before you stop a stranger?
quizzes.why: Excuse me asks for their attention politely.

options: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
quizzes.a: Excuse me. Where is the bank, please?
quizzes.why: Excuse me at the front and please at the end.
Toilets is more than one, so are.

quizzes.q: Keep going. Do not turn. That is ___.
quizzes.why: Straight on means do not change direction.

quizzes.q: Two streets meet there. It is the ___.
quizzes.why: A corner is where two streets meet.

quizzes.q: They said: turn left at the bank. What do you say back?
quizzes.why: Saying it back checks you understood before you walk away.

quizzes.q: Why do you say the answer back?
quizzes.why: A nod is not checking. Saying it back is.

quizzes.q: They spoke too fast. You say ___.
quizzes.why: Asking them to slow down is normal and not rude.

quizzes.q: You heard nothing at all. You say ___.
quizzes.why: Again please asks for the whole thing one more time.

quizzes.q: It is a long way from here. It is ___.
quizzes.why: Far means a long way. Near means close.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: The checking half matters more than the asking half
teacherNotes.note: Most courses teach the question and stop. A learner who asks well and then cannot follow the answer is no better off. Pattern 3 and Practice 4 are the ones that change what happens in the street. Do not skip them for time.

teacherNotes.type: Teach left and right with hands, not words
teacherNotes.note: A learner translating left in their head while somebody talks will lose the rest of the sentence. Get them pointing as the other person speaks. A wrong hand gets corrected on the spot, which is exactly what you want.

teacherNotes.type: Excuse me is a whole move
teacherNotes.note: Wait to be looked at, say excuse me, ask, listen, say it back, thank them. Practise the sequence, not the phrase. A learner who has done it six times in a room will do it once in a street.

teacherNotes.type: Asking twice is the skill, not a failure
teacherNotes.note: Many adults will walk away lost rather than ask a second time. Say plainly that asking again is normal and that native speakers do it constantly. That sentence is worth as much as the vocabulary.

selfAssessment.statement: I can name places in a town.
I can ask where a place is.
I can understand left and right.
I can say the answer back to check it.
I can ask you to show me.
I can read directions on a page.

assignment.title: Ask the way, and check the answer
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Ask the way to three places.
Start each one with excuse me.
Then say three answers back as questions.
2. Write four lines of directions to your home.
Listen back before you finish. Could a stranger follow them?
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
